question: Should Gateway origin policy allow `chrome-extension://*`, and if yes should that live inside `allowedOrigins` or a separate constrained pattern surface?
rationale: This changes a Gateway browser-origin authorization boundary and the current config contract treats `allowedOrigins` as exact full origins except for global `*`; automation should not choose the permanent wildcard grammar or extension-origin trust model.

options.title: Approve constrained extension pattern policy
options.body: Add a narrow, documented, audited pattern rule for extension origins with explicit negative tests and no generic prefix matching beyond the approved grammar.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Land or sponsor exact custom-scheme origin fixes and accept that changing Chrome extension IDs remain an operator config task.

options.title: Reject extension-wide trust
options.body: Document that trusting every Chrome extension origin is too broad for Gateway origin authorization and keep `chrome-extension://*` unsupported.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained extension pattern policy
recommendation.body: Add a narrow, documented, audited pattern rule for extension origins with explicit negative tests and no generic prefix matching beyond the approved grammar.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and hardened the Gateway browser-origin policy surface, making him the strongest history-backed owner for this security-boundary choice.
